..
KEY MESSAGE 1...
It seems another period of active and wet weather is upon the
region. The upper pattern features a continued flatten ridge
aloft over the eastern CONUS with another shortwave trough
approaching the region. The patten sets up a storm track across
the Midwest and into the Upper OH Valley. This will keep a
series of shortwave trough approaching the area through the
middle of next next week. 

Addressing the Saturday night into Sunday threat, showers and
thunderstorms are tracking across Ohio and mainly sliding just
south of the forecast area. There are some scattered development
tracking just north of I-70 but this rainfall is not expected to
be impactful. The amount of instability is below 500 J/Kg and
mainly a flood threat is expected at this point through dawn. 

By the 10Z to 16Z period additional development is expected into
central Ohio with PWATs at 1.8 to 2.0. Plenty of moisture to 
work with and the NBM giving a 90th percentile amount through 
the day on Sunday looks to be around 0.75 to 1.50 as a swath of 
heavy rainfall lines up from just south of PIT and south into 
the WV counties in the north. The 90th has potential given the 
amount of moisture in the air. The only hindrance in reaching 
these values is the amount of instability available. This looks
to be a 24 hour probability and would lead to at least a few 
issues through the day. On another note, the CAMs and ensembles 
are not handling the amount of rain potential very well, 
although the track seems to have slide south increasing 
confidence in a southern Flash Flood Watch and one may be needed
for the next round since the soils would be primed. 

The severe threat for Sunday seems to focus mainly in the
morning with the initial rainfall as profiles would show deep 
saturation and no dry air. If a storm does develop, the main 
threat would be damaging winds. The Sunday night period will 
feature another round of rain crossing the southern portion of 
the forecast area. This third or even fourth round of rain would
begin to cause some concern in flooding across the area south 
of Pittsburgh. The Monday period will feature some showers 
across the area but will be concerning given the amount of 
rainfall since Saturday night. It seems that even Monday will 
need to be monitored for the potential of flooding. 

Following a brief lowering of rain chances early Monday, it'll 
remain active into the middle part of the week. While the setup 
doesn't appear to favor heightened flash flooding concerns any given 
day, long duration accumulation has the potential to be more 
notable. Latest NBM 48 hour QPF from Monday morning - Wednesday 
morning has the highest values south of Pittsburgh where a slow 
moving/stalled boundary is progged to be. Location of that will be 
paramount for who gets the bulk of the rain, and right now, most 
ensembles place it south of Pittsburgh. Mean values are around 1.25-
1.5" there, and 90th percentile values up to 2-3.5". Farther north, 
the mean is much less at 0.5-0.75" with the high end around 1.5-2". 
There are even some solutions (mostly a southward displaced 
boundary) in which the northern part of the area sees very 
little rain. While this all told wouldn't pose as much a threat 
for flash flooding, areal flooding and river flooding chances 
may increase especially if the high-end potential is realized. 
The primary way to realize that high end potential would be to 
be positioned immediately north of the stationary boundary with 
overrunning, and/or on the northwest side of a developing 
coastal low. Should the stationary boundary be too far south or 
the coastal low to far east, these threats would not be 
realized. The area with highest potential for impacts will be 
south of Pittsburgh and will need continued monitoring into 
early week.

KEY MESSAGE 2...
The other story of the week is going to be the much cooler air 
in place with several days where the highs may not get out of 
the 50s for some. Surface high pressure across New England will 
induce stout, prolonged east-northeast flow locally. NBM probs 
for daytime highs exceeding 65F is basically a 50/50 shot from 
the ridges to Pittsburgh, then a bit higher farther west, all 
that with a summertime-biased NBM and likely a bit too high even
at that; AI guidance and some deterministic models are running 
a handful of degrees cooler. Normal highs are in the low 70s and
lows in the low 50s throughout next week, so while lows should 
be right around normal, we could be looking at highs some 10 
degrees below.
